ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 sections 21.1-21.4 (significant control register); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Quebec Act to Establish a Register of Enterprises (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (money laundering provisions), as amended by S.C. 2019, c.13.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Authentication Services, Global Affairs Canada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (provincial certificate issued by the Registrar or certified by Quebec Ministry of Justice Authentication Office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the Canadian province of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada Authentication Services)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the resolution is executed outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC examination for politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEPs) in conformity with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; obligatory screening against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (under the Special Economic Measures Act), the United Nations suppressed sanctions list (regulations under the United Nations Act), the OFAC SDN List (for US-dollar clearing exposure), and the EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists if transactions involve those jurisdictions. Screening must be repeated prior to any changes in UBO composition, upon large wire transfers, and at least annually under a risk-based AML compliance program.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Name Reservation and Registration Portal (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the corporate name must be in French. A non-French name is permitted only with prior authorization from the Office québécois de la langue française. The name must be distinct in the enterprise register, must not be identical or mislead similarly to an existing name, and must follow the statutory linguistic transliteration doctrine (no transliteration if it amounts to a non-French version of a French name).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation may be renewed once for a further 90-day period by filing a renewal request with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and paying the statutory fee. If the name is refused, the applicant may submit an administrative review request within 30 days of the written refusal, attaching a satisfactory explanation of distinctiveness and a revised proposed name. If the review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the civil court having jurisdiction in Quebec to order the registrar to record the name. Any appeal must be filed with the competent division of the Court of Quebec or the Superior Court of Quebec, depending on the nature of the refusal, and legal counsel must observe the ninety-day appeals deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally not accepted as the sole registered office in Quebec, because the Quebec Enterprise Registrar requires a physical address within Quebec where the constitution and corporate records are maintained and where legal process may be served. A virtual location may be used as a supplementary administrative mailing address only if a physical registered office is separately maintained. For a marine insurance surveyor, provincial compliance may additionally require a physical office for the general corporate record and for insurance-related professional liability documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 15% over the first 12 months based on the low-risk AML tier, occasional regulator follow-up on marine insurance claims activity, and the Registrar's practice of conducting random address-verification checks for professional service corporations. The likelihood increases to approximately 30% if the registered office is also used for public-facing survey activities or if an insurance claims complaint triggers regulatory inquiry.

Registered office physical address service in Quebec (first 12 months)
Legal drafting of articles, by-laws, share terms, and UBO compliance manual
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for small-cap professional service corporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, articles of incorporation and corporate constitution provisions; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (publicity declarations); Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services, CQLR c. D-9.2 (claims adjuster firm certification for marine hull and cargo survey operations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), legal publicity registry and incorporation service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) submitted through REQ's online incorporation counter
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; a nominal share capital based on 100 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share is recommended. Subscriptions must be paid into the incorporating lawyer's trust account pending issuance of the certificate of incorporation; no escrow account is required by the QBCA for cash subscriptions, but funds may not be used by the corporation before the certificate issues.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the sole incorporator for 100 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share, fully paid, is accepted and allotted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at 1000 Rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Suite 2500, Montréal, Québec H3B 4W5, and that corporate records shall be kept there. RESOLVED, that [Principal Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Counsel Name] Corporate Secretary, and [Treasurer Name] Treasurer, each at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED, that the fiscal year ends December 31; management is authorized to file registry declarations, open bank accounts, and secure the AMF certificate for marine claims survey operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online reserved-name service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ's online counter and submit a name requisition for at least three semantic variants of the proposed corporate name bearing the legal designation 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Limitée' and a preponderant French component; pay the CAD 39 fee and obtain a name reservation valid for 90 days. The name must not contravene the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and must identify the marine survey activity, e.g., a French or bilingual firm name containing 'marine surveyor' or an equivalent expression.
required_dossiers: Request for name search submitted online
Declaration by the incorporator identifying proposed names in order of preference
Written authorization of the incorporating attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused for resemblance, submit a fresh requisition with new distinctive elements within the same 90-day period; an administrative review of the refusal may be requested from the REQ and subsequently appealed in the civil division of the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Incorporation Filings (Legal Persons Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically sign the Articles of Incorporation via the REQ's online portal using the reserved name; attach the registered-office declaration locating the registered office at 1000 Rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Suite 2500, Montréal, Québec H3B 4W5; pay the combined duty of approximately CAD 400 (USD 300) by credit card or counsel trust transfer. On approval, the REQ files the articles and issues the Certificate of Constitution, which is conclusive proof of the corporation's existence from the date of issuance.
required_dossiers: Registered office address declaration with Quebec postal address
Consent of the sole director to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is set aside for incompleteness, re-submit corrected articles within 30 days under the same reservation; if the REQ issues a written query, counsel submits a written response electronically or by registered mail, and any refused registration attracts a pro-rata fee credit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax and Payroll Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Fichier des entreprises) jointly with the Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate is issued, confirm the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) transmitted by the REQ; register program accounts for GST/HST, QST, corporate income tax, and payroll source deductions through Revenu Québec's online form LM-1 and the CRA's Form RC1. Attest anticipated annual revenues, first fiscal year end of December 31, and the registered-office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Add or correct accounts by filing an amending declaration on Revenu Québec's enterprise space; any erroneous QST or GST credit can be reversed via an equivalent adjustment page; late-registration inquiries may be waivable where good-faith error is demonstrated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Organization and Legal Publicity Filing of Officers and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Publicity of Legal Persons Counter; executed internally at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational written meeting, adopt governance by-laws and the corporate seal, maintain the securities register, and certify the minutes in the minute book. File with the REQ the declaration of directors and officers, indicating the chief executive, secretary, treasurer, and their powers for the benefit of third persons, within 60 days of constitution; retain the attestation issued by the REQ.
required_dossiers: First board written resolutions and minutes
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Share certificate book and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publicity declaration is queried, cancel and re-file the corrected version or file an amending declaration; rectifications take effect as of the date of filing before the REQ and any prior inconsistency shall be described in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Marine Insurance Survey Firm Authorization (AMF Claims Adjuster Certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), Dossiers d'inscription Section, online certificates portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the Corporation intends to act as a marine insurance surveyor inspecting hull and cargo damage and adjusting claims, the AMF classifies the activity as claims adjustment under the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services. Submit the firm recognition application, remit the administration fee, and attach corporate formation history; the designated responsible officer and every surveyor must hold an individual claims adjuster certificate or be exempt by the AMF. Provide professional liability insurance covering marine risks.
required_dossiers: Application for firm recognition following AMF guide
Certificate of incorporation and up-to-date statement from REQ
Individual claims adjuster certificates for natural persons in charge
Professional liability insurance certificate with marine clause
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the AMF's queries within the indicated delay, typically 30 days; any refusal is contestable before the Tribunal administratif des marchés financiers (TAMF) within 60 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupancy Licensing, Fire Safety, and Environmental Compliance Exemption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Borough administration of Montréal (Permis de commerce) with regulatory acknowledgement of the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), and Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal commercial occupancy permit for the office; obtain a fire safety attestation from the building owner under the Quebec Fire Safety Code with extinguisher inspection and exit plans; declare the office as no-impact office use to the RBQ and register the workplace with CNESST under the occupational health and safety program; retain the MELCCFP waste characterization confirming no environmental authorization trigger.
required_dossiers: Municipal application form from the borough office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the borough questions the permit, provide the certificate of address from the lease and an architect's floor plan; if the fire safety attestation is not accepted, obtain the RBQ's inspection under the Fire Safety Act within 20 days and re-file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), Directorate of Registration and Obligations; municipal borough of Montréal for commercial occupancy; no separate provincial industrial license applies to office-based marine survey services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Firm recognition certificate for claims adjustment specialized in marine hull and cargo surveying (carte d'expert en sinistres de la firme) issued under the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services, CQLR c. D-9.2

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the undertaking is an office-based marine inspection and claims survey service; no EIA report or ministerial authorization is triggered under the Environmental Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, because the activity is not a listed industrial installation or contaminant discharge source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable to the core activity; office sanitary wastewater discharges to the Montréal municipal sewer under municipal by-law limits (pH 6.0–11.0, BOD5 300 mg/L, TSS 300 mg/L); no VOC point sources; damaged-cargo residues and survey waste, if any, must be transferred to licensed carriers under the Regulation respecting residual materials and the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 46 and r. 40.2).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety attestation for the office suite meeting Quebec Fire Safety Code requirements, including annual extinguisher inspection, illuminated exits, and fire separation plans; structural load verification of the records vault by the building engineer; CNESST registration of the workplace and occupational health and safety policy under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1; civil defense evacuation plan coordinated with the building's emergency measures program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; for Québec provincial sales tax, Revenu Québec at https://www.revenuquebec.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident corporation doing business in Canada obtains a 15-character Business Number (BN), which serves as the TIN. Steps: (1) incorporate federally or provincially, or register extra-provincially with Corporations Canada or the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (2) register for CRA tax accounts through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or Form RC1, supplying corporate registration documents and directors' information; (3) where the corporation carries on a Québec commercial activity, also obtain the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and register for GST/HST and QST accounts with Revenu Québec via 'Register for Tax Services' in the Québec enterprise register; (4) open CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec clic ReQ UT account; (5) keep BN and NEQ references on all invoices and customs documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. A Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act is inherently classified as a taxable corporation, and entity-level taxation is mandatory. Available elections include the non-resident corporation's subsection 216(1) Income Tax Act election for net Canadian property income, section 85 rollover elections for reorganization transactions, and certain provincial election mechanisms, but none changes the default corporation classification or grants pass-through eligibility. Hybrid mismatch rules in Income Tax Act sections 12.4 and 18.4 are mandatory statutory anti-avoidance provisions, not elective classification regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and Québec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in total taxable supplies by a non-resident carrying on business in Canada in any single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four quarters; QST: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Québec for the QST small-supplier threshold. Services supplied to non-resident insurers may nevertheless be zero-rated, but registration remains advisable to recover input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate is in force at either the federal or Québec level. CRA accepts electronic invoices containing the prescribed statutory information under Excise Tax Act section 230; electronic GST/HST return filing is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1,500,000. Revenu Québec requires electronic filing of QST returns and prescribed invoices, but does not operate a government pre-approval or digital stamping clearance system for routine invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A marine claims survey service is zero-rated as an exported service only when the recipient is a non-resident who is not a GST/HST registrant and the service is not supplied in connection with real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or intangible personal property for use in Canada. If the vessel or cargo is physically present in Canadian territory at the time of inspection, the supply is ordinarily taxable at 5% GST and 9.975% QST unless a specific statutory exception applies. The commercial documentation must establish the foreign ownership of the insured risk, the non-resident status of the insurer, and the absence of a Canadian situs for the property surveyed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canadian Export Reporting System record) where goods are exported
Bill of Lading or original shipping evidence for vessel or cargo movements
Inward remittance certificate or bank wire confirmation showing foreign-currency receipt within the contractual period
Executed marine claims survey agreement and survey report identifying the insured object, survey location, and cause of damage
Certificate of non-resident status or declaration from the foreign underwriter or reinsurer
GST/HST and QST invoice with zero-rating notation and supporting place-of-supply analysis
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess invalid zero-rated export claims within the normal four-year reassessment period, or indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is present. A reassessment will claw back claimed input tax credits, charge GST/QST, and impose interest. Under Excise Tax Act section 285.1, the civil penalty is the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the tax amount for false statements; gross negligence penalties can also apply; fraudulent conduct carries criminal liability with significant fines and imprisonment. Revenu Québec applies parallel QST penalties, including interest and penalties under the Québec Taxation Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and FINTRAC; Canada maintains no central foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible for both current and capital-account transactions; Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and does not impose capital controls, exchange-rate ceilings, or limitations on profit remittance; dividends, management fees, and loan repayments may be transferred freely, subject only to normal tax withholding and anti-money-laundering verification
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts; there is no obligation to repatriate, surrender, or convert foreign-currency proceeds; Canadian exporters may retain funds in foreign-currency bank accounts, and all conversion decisions are commercial

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — European EMIs and offshore digital payment platforms are not recognized as banks under the Bank Act; they cannot accept deposits or issue Canadian bank accounts without operating as registered money-service businesses (MSBs) under FINTRAC; cross-border payment fintech (including Wise) may be used as payment corridors for low-value transfers, but major corporate treasury functions must remain with a Tier-1 Canadian chartered bank
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video identity verification is generally accepted under FINTRAC guidance; however, Tier-1 banks may require at least one director or authorized signatory to attend an in-person or video interview; for a wholly foreign-owned Canadian corporation in Quebec, the ultimate beneficial owner or a designated Canadian-resident director should be prepared to appear at a Canadian branch or via bank-approved video conferencing

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial ownership exceeding 25% of the operating corporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Province of Quebec Registraire des entreprises certificate, identifiable shareholder register, Canadian agent for service of process confirmation, beneficial-ownership and control chart, notarized corporate resolutions, and a global entity diagram including the foreign parent's incorporation documents and good-standing certificate

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial high-value wire injection with non-Canadian source-of-funds documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement, board resolution authorizing capital injection, foreign bank statement of the remitting account, source-of-wealth questionnaire for the ultimate beneficial owner, and a signed warranty letter confirming no third-party directional funding or proxy capital

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine insurance surveying business classification perceived as insurance brokerage or unlicensed underwriting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provincial licensing certificate or exemption letter issued by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for marine surveying activities, detailed scope-of-services letter, professional liability policy summary, and client contracts confirming the firm acts solely as an independent surveyor and not as an insurer or intermediary

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant incoming capital injections must be executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the foreign parent's bank into the Canadian operating account using the purpose code 'Capital Subscription – Injection to Paid-in Capital' (statement reference: CAD or USD); the bank will require the corporate resolution, subscription agreement, and UBO declaration; no Bank of Canada / OSFI prior approval is needed, but FINTRAC reporting thresholds apply and the wire must match the authorized share capital record in the Quebec corporate registry
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements from the Canadian corporation to marine claim payers, underwriters, subcontracted surveyors, or international trade counterparties are cleared via (a) SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency and cross-border CAD wires, (b) Lynx (Canada's high-value real-time gross settlement system) for domestic CAD payments, and (c) Commercial Letters of Credit issued through Tier-1 Canadian chartered banks for insured marine cargo survey engagements; all outbound wires require transaction-level KYC and a proper purpose code such as 'Payment for Professional Surveying Services' or 'Reimbursement of Claim Disbursement'
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore non-deliverable forwards (limited to non-CAD counterparties as a complementary hedge only; CAD is deliverable under normal market conditions)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Enterprise Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the enterprise registration; a declaration must be filed at least once every twelve months.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty plus administrative interest; two consecutive years without a declaration may result in REQ strike-off after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by the Director after a default notice and cure period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue/asset threshold applies to a CBCA or QBCA private corporation. An annual independent audit is mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer or distributing corporation; otherwise a private marine surveyor can waive appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution for that fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS, CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) is available for this non-reporting private surveyor corporation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec enterprise-register filings require confirmation of any individuals with significant control (direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of voting rights, or ability to appoint/remove directors). Share transfers must be posted in the company's securities register and reported to REQ in the annual declaration or on a 30-day change filing; if none exists, the declaration must affirm no individual with significant control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 350 per year for Quebec registered office and corporate agent filing services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 9,000 per year if an independent CPA audit is required; nil if the unanimous shareholder audit waiver is renewed annually.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific statutory tax holiday for marine insurance surveying. Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may access the federal small business deduction (9% federal rate on the first C$500,000 of active business income) and Quebec's small business reduction, producing an approximate 20.5% combined rate on eligible small-business income. Refundable SR&ED investment tax credits and Quebec innovation credits can further reduce effective tax. Quebec offers refundable tax credits for research and innovation that surveyors performing hull and cargo claims analytics may qualify for if work includes software or testing methods.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, transmitted through CRA Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) or approved third-party EDI/XML software. The Quebec component is prepared on Form CO-17 and remitted via Revenu Québec's electronic portal ('E-services' / Mon Dossier d'entreprise).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Both T2 and CO-17 must be filed no later than six months after the corporate fiscal year-end. A Quebec business corporation resident in Quebec is required to file both returns. Payments of instalments for Quebec and federal corporate taxes generally follow quarterly/ monthly rules based on prior-year tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), incorporation jurisdiction, registered office address, fiscal period start/end, and principal business activity code. For a marine claims survey corporation, enter ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a permanent establishment (PE) in Quebec must identify the PE address and appoint a resident agent for service. Canadian tax residency is determined by management and control; a foreign-incorporated surveyor managed from Quebec must indicate 'resided in Canada' and complete the full T2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income: gross insurance-survey revenue, deductibles, wages, subcontracting costs, survey vessel or vehicle expenses, travel, professional fees, and capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents earning Canadian-source business income through a PE must allocate revenue and expenses between the Canadian PE and home office. Transfer pricing documentation is required for cross-border management fees, shared technology, and intercompany survey referrals.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate provincial/federal taxable income after loss carryovers and all applicable deductions. Federal and Quebec non-capital loss carryforwards extend up to 20 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Canadian-source income attributable to the PE is reported. Loss carryovers are limited to the portion of losses incurred within Canada. Attach NR301 and foreign tax credit schedules if treaty benefits reduce Canadian tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Part VIII – Federal Tax / Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes federal income tax at 38%, less the 10% provincial abatement and 13% federal general rate reduction, yielding the effective 15% general federal rate. Then subtracts small business deduction, SR&ED investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation claiming treaty exemption for its Canadian PE income must include a Form NR301 and supporting residency certificate. The 10% provincial abatement is unavailable if the corporation is not resident in a participating province; Quebec-resident corporations are entitled to the Quebec abatement via the integrated T2/CO-17 settlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under section 162(1) is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months), with an increased 10% penalty for a second late filing within three years. Arrears interest accrues daily at prescribed rates. Quebec imposes equivalent late-filing penalties, a C$25 administrative fee, and denial of deductions or refunds until return is filed. For aggressive evasion, gross-negligence penalty is 50% of understated tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (Form CO-17), filed solely with Revenu Québec. The CO-17 integrates the provincial tax computation and, under the federal-provincial collection agreement, Quebec administers the Part XIII federal withholding only where specifically delegated.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end for both federal and Quebec returns. If a corporation carries on no activity, a nil return is still due within six months of the year-end. Quebec corporations must also file the separate Registre des entreprises (REQ) annual declaration under the Business Corporations Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ), business number, business address, sector code, and fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a PE in Quebec must obtain an NEQ before filing and indicate the Quebec establishment address. Foreign directors acting as Quebec registrants may require a Quebec-issued authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.name: Quebec corporate return identification

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute Quebec taxable income from Canadian and Quebec active business income, adjusting for provincial differences (e.g., Quebec-specific political contributions, specialized loss carryovers).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident should allocate income to the Quebec PE following arm's-length internal pricing. Cross-border marine survey fees charged by a non-resident head office must satisfy Part XIII withholding and Quebec transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Lines 224–251 – Tax Rates and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec general corporate rate of 11.5%; small business deduction and investment tax credits are computed on Schedule P.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief claimed federally on Form NR301 is also respected by Quebec only if the treaty applies under Quebec domestic adoption. Non-resident corporations should attach the federal T2 and Schedule 1 to substantiate the consistency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing in Quebec: 5% of the balance due plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failures attract 20% for chronic non-compliance; interest compounded daily at Quebec's prescribed redemption rate. Willful omission carries civil penalties of up to C$50,000 and penal fines under the Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under federal Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder. No separate Quebec provincial dividend withholding tax is applied on the same remittance because Part XIII is a federal tax. Treaty relief can reduce the rate to 5% for an U.S. parent owning at least 10% of voting shares, 15% for portfolio investors, and analogous rates under other comprehensive bilateral DTAs (e.g., 15% for Germany, 10% for France under varying conditions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding, the Canadian payer must collect a properly completed NR301 'Statement of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits' from the non-resident beneficial owner before or at time of payment. The non-resident recipient must obtain a current residence certificate (e.g., IRS Form 6166 in the US, HMRC Form RES in the UK) issued by its home tax authority and provide it to the payer or CRA upon request. Quebec corporations are bound by the federal treaty network. If withholding was remitted at the full statutory rate, the non-resident may file Form NR7 to apply for a refund within two years. All treaty documentation must be retained for six years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties and interest is also 25% Part XIII. Interest paid at arm's length to a non-resident lender is exempt from Canadian withholding if it is not 'participating debt interest' and the lender is not a specified shareholder. Treaty rates are generally lower: for royalties under the Canada-U.S. DTA, 10% for industrial/patent/trademark royalties and 0% for certain copyright and computer-software royalties; interest is 0% for non-participating arm's-length debt. Under most Canadian tax treaties, industrial royalties and interest are capped at 10%, but arm's-length interest often falls under a domestic exemption.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Form T106 reporting applies to reportable non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents that exceed C$1,000,000 in aggregate per year. Local File and Master File documentation must be prepared contemporaneously when an audit-level risk of transfer-pricing adjustments exists; CbC notification is mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue over C$750 million. Documentation must include functional analysis, economic analysis, comparable searches, and prices/margins for every controlled cross-border service or reinsurance arrangement. Marine survey corp. commonly transacts with foreign insurers, underwriters, or affiliated survey companies and must satisfy these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies OECD/G20 economic substance principles through statutory GAAR (section 245 Income Tax Act) and the transfer-pricing recharacterization power (section 247). No standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) registry exists in Quebec, but a corporate entity with no real or qualified personnel, minimal presence, and no board or management activity in Quebec may be disregarded as a conduit; treaty benefits can be denied under 'beneficial owner' and 'permanent establishment' clauses. The CRA and Revenu Québec assess commercial reality, local decision-making, personnel, assets, office premises and business purpose. A marine insurance surveyor must maintain an operational office in Quebec or, if foreign-owned, demonstrate meaningful and substantive survey activity inside Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of gross survey fee revenues received via underwriter wire or Wise, fabrication of lapsed expenses, off-book invoicing, or misreporting corporate income in T2/CO-17. Failing to disclose a foreign bank account used for underwriting payments also constitutes criminal tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and forfeiture of property related to the offence. Civil gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of understated tax; interest on unpaid balances. Quebec penalties up to C$50,000 on the corporation and the registration may be cancelled by Revenu Québec.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act and section 1018 of the Quebec Taxation Act for corporate tax, interest, and penalties when they direct, authorize, or acquiesce in false filings. Directors can face personal criminal conviction, travel restrictions, asset seizure, and veil-piercing in Quebec civil proceedings where the corporation is an instrumentality of shareholder fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Shell Conduit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length service fees or inflated management fees paid to a related non-resident survey corporation with no actual personnel; failure to document intercompany transactions or file Form T106; routing premium income through an offshore entity lacking Canadian substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may re-assess at the arm's-length price and also impose a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net understatement where the amount understated exceeds C$5 million or reasonable basis requirement is not met. GAAR can deny the tax benefit and levy penalties of up to 50% of the benefit. Additionally, denial of Part XIII exemption for foreign-source allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in a sham transfer-pricing arrangement risk civil joint liability for re-assessed tax, plus criminal exposure for tax evasion if false documentation is presented. Canadian courts may pierce the corporate veil to attach personal assets where the company is a mere facade and used for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold, Remit, and Report Non-Resident Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Quebec insurer or surveying company pays dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent or beneficiary without withholding Part XIII tax; failure to file Form NR4-Associated Statements, Form NR301, or Form T5/T4 for prescribed payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of the unremitted withholding amount, plus daily interest and a 20% civil penalty for repeated failure. Non-remittance is a criminal offence under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act, with fines up to C$25,000 and imprisonment up to two years. Quebec QST and payroll remittances carry distinct penal assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are strictly personally liable for unremitted withholding taxes; no defence of good faith is available unless they exercised due diligence to prevent the failure. CRA issues director liability certificates that become judicial judgments, allowing garnishment of personal bank accounts and real property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership / Shell Company Framework
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a corporate entity with nominee shareholders or undisclosed principals; having no operational activity in Quebec while receiving underwriting commission; failing to file the annual return of beneficial owners with the Quebec Registraire des entreprises; violating Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act for refusing client due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to C$1 million for corporations for AML/beneficial ownership omissions; criminal sanctions and fines for willful contravention. Revenu Québec can strike the company from the register, rendering contracts unenforceable; directors then face civil liability for corporate obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing occurs in Quebec under civil law when the company is created to commit fraud or misuse corporate personality. Directors may be ordered to personally restore assets misappropriated, receive travel bans, and are amenable to extradition for cross-border tax fraud or money laundering. Individual officers can be imprisoned for up to 10 years under the Income Tax Act after indictment.
